kicker: Steel pipes & tubes · sales vs margins, Q2 FY27
title: Pipe makers sold more; freight and tariffs took the margin
title_em: freight and tariffs took the margin
dek: Five of seven listed steel-pipe makers grew Q2 FY27 sales but lost EBITDA margin; four blamed freight, fuel or US tariffs. Welspun Corp, with US orders priced through FY29, widened its margin 2.1 points.

legend.c: Down: freight, fuel or tariffs cited

stats.label: Welspun Corp's order book
stats.note: About $5.2 bn, a record, with its US line-pipe capacity booked through FY29.

stats.label: US tariff on Ratnamani's exports
stats.note: It ships duty-paid, so freight and duty hit its margin: 14.0% from 17.7%.

stats.label: Jindal Saw's Q2 EBITDA
stats.note: Down from ₹482 cr on delayed Saudi shipments and logistics costs.

read: Order books are full; margins now turn on who pays freight and duty, so Q3 shipping costs are the number to watch.
sources: Vantage analysis of Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE and Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Vantage sector intel, 21 Nov 2026
notes: Sales growth and EBITDA margin (operating EBITDA over revenue from operations) are from filed Q2 FY27 and Q2 FY26 results, consolidated except Venus Pipes and Scoda Tubes (standalone), as computed by Vantage; company-reported margins can differ (Ratnamani reported 16.3% including other items). Causes are what management cited on Q2 FY27 calls: logistics costs and delayed Saudi job-work shipments (Jindal Saw), freight and duty on duty-paid US exports under a 50% tariff (Ratnamani), export freight and fuel (Venus), power, fuel and freight (Scoda). Hi-Tech Pipes' margin dip came with lower EBITDA per tonne on 32% volume growth. Maharashtra Seamless (inventory-valuation hit) and Hariom Pipe (sales up 65% after a plant restart) are left out as one-offs, and Goodluck India because its standalone and consolidated margin moves disagree.
